Accounts.settledFines memberId next |> List.skip (Accounts.settledFines memberId library |> List.length)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Two new domain rules are added: oldest-first allocation with paid, part-paid and unpaid status, and which fines a payment settled. Both are decided in Tier 2 (Accounts.allocation, Accounts.settledFines, Payments.pay). Tier 3 Views only maps the Tier 2 FineStatus onto a view union. The CLI only turns view cases into text ('paid', 'paid X of Y', 'unpaid', '(settled ...)'). Neither re-derives anything. The decision not to write off small remainders is also stated in Tier 2 (Payments.fs doc comment), not in an outer tier.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No effect is added below Tier 4. The change also removes an existing clock read from Tier 2 (`PaidOn = DateOnly.FromDateTime DateTime.Today` becomes a `today` parameter). Today's date now reaches Payments.pay from the Clock port through the existing `commit` coordination. Allocation and settlement are pure functions of Library. Persistence still goes through the Store port via commit.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Allocation order and fine status have one definition (Accounts.allocation). settledFines is built on it, Payments.pay uses settledFines, and Views uses allocation. Nothing copies the rule. `owed` and `allocation` each sum the payments, but both are in the same Tier 2 module and agree: the total allocated always equals min(paid, total fines). No literal policy value is restated.

| Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The core waiver rules live in Tier 2: which fine can be waived, approver required, paid part kept, waived fine taking no more payments and leaving what is owed (Waivers.waive, Accounts.countedAmount, Accounts.allocation's Waived case). The change also moves the borrowing block out of the CLI into Tier 2 Loans.borrow via Accounts.isBlocked, which fixes an existing violation. One gap remains: Tier 2's Waived status carries only an amount, so Tier 3 Views decides with its own `paid > 0m` check whether a waived fine was 'paid in part' or 'nothing paid'. For unwaived fines Tier 2 makes that same distinction itself (PaidInPart vs Unpaid via `applied > 0m`). This is a local re-derivation of a status distinction in Tier 3. It does not contradict Tier 2.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The waive use case gets today's date from the Clock port through `commit` and persists through the Store port. Waivers.waive is pure and returns the new Library. Serialization of the new Waiver field stays in the Tier 4 persistence adapter (JsonCodec). Tier 1/2 has no new I/O, clock or console use. The CLI no longer calls ports.Store.Load() for borrow, which removes a presentation-to-persistence decision path.

evidence.quote: | Some waiver -> (fine, Waived(waiver.PaidBefore, waiver.Approver)), remaining - min remaining waiver.PaidBefore

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The change removes an existing duplicate: the CLI's hard-coded `fines - paid >= 5.00m` copy of the blocking balance. Borrowing now uses Accounts.isBlocked, which uses Policy.blockingBalance and the new waiver-aware `owed`, so the two can no longer drift. How much a waived fine counts is defined once (countedAmount → PaidBefore). Allocation uses the same PaidBefore value inline, in the same Tier 2 module, and agrees with it. PaidBefore is a snapshot taken from allocation at waiver time. Payments are append-only, so it stays consistent. The Views `paid > 0m` check is scored under ARC-REV-01. It restates no policy value.
